lxc_81708deb0aed88e4.text: The Night of the Radishes in Oaxaca, the Olney Pancake Race, the Gävle Goat, the Guérewol in Niger, the Monkey Buffet Festival in Lopburi, and fire-walking on Beqa bring people together in very different ways.

lxc_df919a37b6e9dd1e.text: Looking at where, when, what, and why helps us understand each tradition.

lxc_84b92cecbb42a1b5.text: The Night of the Radishes takes place every December 23 in Oaxaca, Mexico.

lxc_c29844ee41937610.text: A radish is a vegetable, but here it becomes material for art.

lxc_3f4684d61b757baf.text: People carve oversized radishes into scenes and compete for prizes.

lxc_174cb935e663fce9.text: The tradition began with farmers who wanted to attract customers at the Christmas market in the main square.

lxc_d8c379ccf82078e5.text: Their carved vegetables helped people notice what they were selling.

lxc_af9d8820bfccb22a.text: The city started the formal competition in 1897.

lxc_639c622a6ed7f349.text: Timing matters because radishes wilt, or lose their fresh shape, soon after cutting.

lxc_d8edfc9d63b160e5.text: The works are shown for only a few hours, and visitors wait in very long lines.

lxc_92614234e1a96547.text: There are also works made from corn husks and dried flowers.

lxc_0df97be617ee5e8c.text: The Olney Pancake Race happens in Olney, Buckinghamshire, England, on Pancake Day, also called Shrove Tuesday.

lxc_2d52526524c75b21.text: They wear a scarf and an apron and carry a frying pan along a course.

lxc_dd24a1a56f6e4f7b.text: They must toss their pancake at the start and the finish.

lxc_4db9b9a5395a7f14.text: The story behind the tradition goes back to 1445.

lxc_c4c5a35f082ba01e.text: A woman was busy making pancakes when she heard the church bells.

lxc_816ad8ac9e4389f3.text: She ran to church still carrying her pan and pancake.

lxc_ca5fe8ec5f9081ab.text: The race remembers that story through action.

lxc_a6179a96c494a1c3.text: Since 1950, Olney and Liberal, Kansas, have held an International Pancake Day race and compared their times.

lxc_33a8dd8e32d26c7b.text: A local tradition therefore also creates a connection between two places.

lxc_2a75b3ddc19567c5.text: In Gävle, Sweden, a giant goat made of straw stands at Castle Square in the centre of the city.

lxc_43dce173269b6688.text: It is a Yule goat, a goat figure connected with the Christmas season.

lxc_832ff93d1fe52836.text: Local community groups build it over two days at the beginning of Advent, the period leading up to Christmas.

lxc_3e450ff3fe8f732f.text: The first Gävle Goat appeared in 1966.

lxc_7ce0c51838ee06fe.text: Since 1986, there have been two goats: one built by the Southern Merchants and another by the Natural Science Club of the School of Vasa.

lxc_76a759a37796029c.text: Here, the main activity is building and displaying a seasonal figure.

lxc_769bbe94095cd5bc.text: A new giant straw goat is put up every year at Castle Square in central Gävle.

lxc_7f53586d3fcccba3.text: The Guérewol is a yearly courtship competition among the Wodaabe Fula people of Niger.

lxc_97d1cb01fee50e97.text: Courtship means trying to attract someone as a possible partner.

lxc_36884c08b6192fa7.text: Young men wear rich decorations and traditional face painting.

lxc_6f2311bb13106522.text: They stand in lines, dance, and sing to win the attention of young women.

lxc_dcf91aa755ac453b.text: The dance is called the Yaake.

lxc_af921436adae1db1.text: The gathering happens when Wodaabe cattle herders meet at the southern edge of the Sahara before moving south for the dry season.

lxc_4b8fd590016bf6a5.text: These herders traditionally move from place to place with their animals.

lxc_3912d0c3a20f72dd.text: A main meeting place is In-Gall in northwest Niger, where there is a festival and a market.

lxc_57e36e4f27cdd0b5.text: The Guérewol lasts about a week, bringing courtship and a seasonal gathering together.

lxc_498d249895abe693.text: The Monkey Buffet Festival happens every year in Lopburi, Thailand, north of Bangkok.

lxc_d1aae0c272351eb8.text: A buffet usually offers a range of food to choose from.

lxc_f6787af5094f718b.text: Here, the food is for local crab-eating macaques, a kind of monkey.

lxc_8bb52b771725e584.text: People give them fruit and vegetables, for example at the Phra Prang Sam Yod temple.

lxc_b79bb8b0f327e05f.text: Sometimes fruit is frozen inside blocks of ice.

lxc_f2813d0e41416136.text: The activity centres on feeding the local monkeys, but sharing a town with them is not always simple.

lxc_ee9f0878eb956a80.text: They caused problems for residents by taking bags, drinks, and food.

lxc_0639bef92f94486d.text: The government started a campaign to catch monkeys and stop them from having babies.

lxc_920a82cc85b816db.text: Beqa is an island in Fiji, about 10 kilometres south of the main island, Viti Levu.

lxc_d1dfcbf8416bf129.text: Several of Beqa’s nine villages are known for fire-walking.

lxc_c5c424c1846c6499.text: In this practice, people walk across hot stones.

lxc_f47e7c485f672bc2.text: In Fiji, it is practised by the Sawau clan, a community group on Beqa.

lxc_7eac7a6d1d97c3f2.text: The approved accounts do not give one yearly date for this tradition.

lxc_a57a55b79f80d5ff.text: They do show its long history as something visitors came to see: it was already a tourist attraction in 1902.

lxc_6152049a597bdecc.text: Fire-walking has different purposes around the world, including healing, faith, and entering adult life.

lxc_76cbb0a11fc86a27.text: Those general purposes do not establish one specific reason for Beqa’s practice.

lxc_28291866b13abea6.text: Here, we can identify a local tradition that also attracts visitors.
